findings.title: Google Meet fallback dereferences an absent destination calendar
findings.body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` when an event has no destination calendar, which is a supported case handled later by the fallback calendar logic. For a Google Meet event, the condition evaluates `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` unconditionally and throws instead of falling back to Cal Video. This breaks booking creation for Google Meet events without a selected destination calendar.

findings.title: Office 365 always creates collective events in the first host calendar
findings.body: Each collective destination is processed with its own credential by `EventManager`, but this service ignores the credential being used and always selects `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. Consequently, when a collective booking has multiple Office 365 hosts, later hosts either attempt to create the event in the first host's calendar using their own token (often failing authorization) or create duplicates there; their configured destination calendars are never used.

findings.title: Lark creation ignores destinations after the first collective host
findings.body: The multi-destination creation loop constructs a Lark service for each destination credential, but `createEvent` always takes the first entry in `event.destinationCalendar`. Thus all Lark host creations target the first host's calendar rather than the destination associated with the credential currently being processed, so collective Lark hosts do not receive their calendar events.

findings.title: CalDAV creation cannot target each collective destination
findings.body: CalDAV event creation filters calendars using only `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. `EventManager` invokes this service once per destination/credential, but the selected destination external ID is not passed into the service, so every invocation targets the first host's calendar. Collective events with multiple CalDAV destinations will therefore be duplicated in or fail against the first destination and omitted from the other hosts' calendars.

findings.title: Recurring collective cancellation deletes only the first calendar reference under every credential
findings.body: For each calendar reference, the recurring-cancellation branch iterates every calendar credential but obtains each recurring booking's reference with `.find(...)`, which always selects only the first calendar reference. With the new multiple-host references, it repeatedly attempts to delete that first event through all credentials and never selects the corresponding references for the other host calendars. Cancelling all remaining instances of a collective recurring booking consequently leaves events on other hosts' calendars (and can issue deletes against unrelated calendars).
